pages.notes: Contents hierarchy viewed: NLP introduction/robotics/challenges/pipeline/core tasks/traditional limits/transformers/LLMs/VLM/VLA.

NLP definition and human-human versus HRI diagram actually viewed. Speech Recognition leads down to Language Understanding inside dashed box; response arrow on upper box edge leads to robot greeting Mary. Do not infer separate algorithm timings from this stylized schematic.

Command Pick up the red ball near the chair decomposed into action pick up, target ball, attribute red and spatial relation near chair. Right list HRI/voice/navigation/planning. Planning and execution follow extraction, not identical to token recognition.

Four challenge examples actually viewed: light lightweight/illuminated ambiguity; ball/bowl accent-related misrecognition; fetch/pick/take contextual synonyms; Great job genuine praise or frustration. Both senses of light shown here can be adjectives, unlike later POS noun/adjective example; do not conflate the two.

Diagram sequence is Human Speech/Text → Pre-Processing → Numerical Representation/Vectorization → Language Understanding → Robot Planning → Robot Action. The text explicitly calls stages conceptual and allows joint internal processing. Listed preprocessing order lowercasing, punctuation removal, tokenization, stopwords, stemming/lemmatization. NLTK full name shown.

Tokenization and list displayed. Vocabulary explicitly unique, but the indented example repeats the; it is an eight-token sequence with seven unique types. Corpus is collection of texts used for training/vocabulary. Dictionary/library analogy is mnemonic, not a storage-type specification. Tokenization alone does not mean the machine has learned semantics.

Stopwords is/a/the, stemming plays/played/playing→play, table studies→studi versus study. Claims faster processing/easier action recognition/lower complexity are task-dependent; removing words can remove relevant relations or negation. Stemming may give nonword; lemma meaningful base.

All 22 code lines and all six right output stages read. Imports nltk/string/word_tokenize/stopwords/WordNetLemmatizer; lower; translate(str.maketrans(empty,empty,string.punctuation)); word_tokenize; set English stopwords; list comprehension preserving order; default noun lemmatize. Output tokens include up and two the; filtered and lemma lists pick/red/ball/near/chair. Displayed code has no print calls, so right report requires a harness. Resource setup not shown.

Code imports PorterStemmer,WordNetLemmatizer; nltk.download(wordnet) relies on earlier import nltk; instantiates both, word=studies, prints Stemmed: studi and Lemmatized: study. Caption Why Lemmatization is better is too broad unless criterion is meaningful lexical base in this example. Corpus download setup side effect is not the mathematical algorithm itself.

Vectorization motivation, pixel analogy, and four methods one-hot/BoW/TF-IDF/Word2Vec-GloVe viewed. Humans understand context clearly is pedagogical contrast, not guarantee all humans resolve ambiguity. Numerical encoding is necessary for computation but not equivalent to semantic correctness.

One-hot and BoW conceptual descriptions actually viewed. Token-level one-hot distinguishes identity, command-level unigram counts discard order/context. Both sparse and high-dimensional; most common is a temporal generalization, not a timeless fact. Count representation is not restricted to binary values.

All OneHotEncoder code and output table viewed. Nested five input rows pick/red/ball/near/chair; sparse_output=False. Alphabetically sorted output columns ball/chair/near/pick/red; row order stays input order. Red annotations distinguish row index 1 from red column index 4. Displayed table is not created by shown fit_transform alone.

CountVectorizer excerpt and complete 3 by 8 table actually viewed. Alphabetical columns ball/blue/box/chair/grab/near/pick/red; rows correspond to three commands. grab and pick have separate columns despite contextual synonym example. fit_transform yields sparse matrix; table formatting not shown.

Normalized term-frequency fraction viewed: term count divided by total terms in document. Documents may be single command or explicitly grouped commands; numerical work must fix boundaries and tokenization. Rarer terms are emphasized only relative to TF and corpus.

IDF=log(total documents/documents containing term), followed by TF-IDF product, actually viewed. Log base unspecified. Document frequency counts presence, not repeated occurrences; zero document frequency makes unsmoothed formula undefined. Ubiquitous terms have zero IDF under this formula.

All TfidfVectorizer code and rounded output table viewed. Same corpus and eight columns; first row .49 ball/chair/near and .37 pick/red; second .68 blue and .52 box/pick; third .68 grab and .52 box/red. These outputs use default smoothed IDF and L2 normalization, not the literal preceding unsmoothed normalized-TF equations. Exact execution and a precise convention qualification are required.

All bullets, cosine equation and 3D schematic viewed. Axes pedagogically named Action/Intention/Context, with pick and fetch rays; no calibrated numerical coordinates. Dense continuous vectors and smaller angle imply higher cosine for nonzero vectors. Most modern, both methods neural networks, cosine used to place words, and more identical meanings are oversimplifications needing exact qualification. GloVe learning objective must not be silently conflated with cosine evaluation.

Language understanding slide viewed; POS and NER named; explicit conceptual separation of vectorization versus meaning extraction, often performed together. Traditional POS-before-NER example versus joint modern modeling does not mandate all architectures.

Exact POS code viewed: download averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng; command capital Pick; word_tokenize(command.lower()); nltk.pos_tag(tokens). Displayed tags pick VB, up RP, the DT, red JJ, ball NN, near IN, the DT, chair NN. Right legend contains DT twice matching repeated tokens, not two distinct classes. Prior imports/resources and report display omitted. No stopword deletion in this code.

Code and output discrepancy actually visible: command2 begins capital Pick and word_tokenize(command2) has no .lower(), while displayed first token is lowercase pick. Both source prose and output label light NN, with intended lightweight reading requiring adjective JJ. Alternative lamp noun interpretation and model dependence must be distinguished; do not claim current runtime reproduces the screenshot before executing.

Entire NER code and tree read: word_tokenize then pos_tag then ne_chunk on Go to Lab3 and meet Mary.; printed tree GPE Lab3/NNP and PERSON Mary/NNP. Right legend S/VB/TO/GPE/NNP/CC/PERSON/punctuation. Source says GPE closest location category; a lab is not necessarily geopolitical and prediction does not establish ontology or physical coordinates. Linked full-code URL resolves only repository root.

Text classification assigns predefined category to entire text; robotics intent classification triggers task class. Examples charger→Navigation, stop immediately→Emergency, lift small crate→Manipulation are task taxonomy, not universal unique labels.

All three task definitions and application examples viewed: sentiment with sarcastic Great job after failure; machine translation for multilingual airports; question answering from a knowledge base with robot mobile interface. Not all QA must be extractive; source example is explicitly knowledge-base answering.

All ASR bullets and five-box diagram viewed. Human speech→ASR speech-to-text→NLP extraction→robot planning→execution. NLP includes preprocessing/vectorization/intent/context. Whisper listed as STT example. ASR task output is a transcript, not by itself a grounded executable plan; source claim no language understanding is task-level simplification, not proof models use no context.

Traditional NLP limitations and cluttered-shelf pronoun example viewed. Listed long instructions, multiple objects, pronouns/references and complex planning. Broad word-by-word and forgetting characterizations must be bounded to systems with limited contextual modeling, not every historical model.

Both attention diagrams actually viewed. Bold strongest schematic arrow links shelf to it in cluttered sentence, robot to it in low-battery sentence. Pale arrows do not provide numerical normalized weights. Text describes surrounding context and attention; common-sense referents are intended examples, not guaranteed inference for every possible world.

Attention can learn importance/relations/focus; C1 slots move action, robot moved object, shelf spatial context. Linking words tracks references and relations. Text-data and parameter scaling described as path to LLMs; not a necessary-and-sufficient threshold definition.

Entire LLM slide and probability table viewed. Definition/tasks/examples, transformer architecture and context→next-token→token-by-token generation. Diagram input pick, candidate up .57, and .35, your .15, it .07 with ellipsis; these four labeled probabilities already sum to 1.14, impossible for mutually exclusive next-token distribution. Preserve as-printed ranking, distinguish explicitly renormalized supplied weight exercise; ellipsis cannot fix excess mass.

All LLM capability/risk bullets and four-box diagram viewed. Flexible commands, conversation, multi-step plans, explanations and clarification. Human command→LLM→robot planning→robot action. Hallucinated information and misunderstood instructions can create unsafe physical actions. Do not turn contested truly understand phrase into objective consciousness claim.

VLM image+text diagram and all bullets viewed. Illustrated ViT produces mapped visual tokens for language processing; not every VLM must have this exact backbone. Mug image plus red-object question; labels mug .78,cup .15,desk .04,pencil .02 with ellipsis (sum .99, possible .01 omitted mass). Listed model names are source examples not current benchmark/ranking.

VLA diagram and text actually viewed. Mug image and pick up instruction; VLM Encoder and Action Prediction Head inside VLA; next embodied state after execution and visual update. Joint angles/end-effector positions discretized in many designs, not universal necessity; movement like a word is representation analogy, not equivalence of safety/semantics. Figure object-label probabilities .65,.10,.04,.02 with ellipses are not calibrated joint coordinates. Examples RT-2 and OpenVLA.
